Check: Does every page include a link to the Harvard Digital Accessibility Policy (most effectively in the footer or another element that repeats on every page)?
Where content cannot be made to conform to the Standards, is it made available in an alternative accessible format?
Do all meaningful images have a descriptive text alternative (alt text)?
How to check: Automated scan (missing alt) + content review of news, event, profile and hero images

Check: Does the alt text provide context on how the image relates to the page content, not just describe the image?
Is the alt text short (usually 1-2 sentences), focused on why the image was chosen rather than every detail?
Does the alt text avoid "image of" / "picture of", but say if the image is a logo, illustration, painting, or cartoon?
Does the alt text avoid duplicating text that is adjacent on the page?
How to check: Content review by a person (e.g. profile headshot next to the person's name)
Notes: Listing photos (people list, service team) keep alt="" because the name sits next to the photo; this departs from live, which repeats the name.

Check: Does the alt text end with a period?
How to check: Automated check of alt attributes + content review

Check: For icons that indicate an action or link to another page (e.g. share buttons), does the text alternative describe the action or what will happen when clicked?
How to check: Template review + screen-reader test (share buttons, icon links in header/footer)

Check: If an image labels a control (such as a button) or provides information (such as a logo), does it contain a meaningful text alternative?

If an icon is provided using an icon font or a CSS background image, is there a text alternative that's read by a screen reader (visually hidden text using a clip technique rather than display:none, or an aria-label on the link)?
Is a purely decorative icon hidden from screen readers with the aria-hidden attribute?
For diagrams and complex images, does the alt text summarize the key meaning and data points, supplemented with adjacent page text and/or a link to the full data where needed?
Are images of text avoided wherever possible (logos excepted), using HTML text styled with CSS instead?
How to check: Template review + content review (hero and graphic images)

Check: Where text appears in or on an image, is that text represented either in the body text or in the alt text (and where an image of text such as a logo is unavoidable, is the same text given as its alt text)?
How to check: Content review by a person (try to highlight the text with your cursor)

Check: Where an image needs additional context or a credit, is that given in a visible caption (separate from the alt text)? (Harvard: "consider")
Does every img element have an alt attribute (never omitted), with an empty (null) alt="" for purely decorative images?
Does each image and media item directly support the information on the page (no images or video added just to "spice up" a page)?
Is each visual section heading identified in code as a heading (h1-h6), not just styled to look bigger and bolder?
Is there only one H1 per page?

Are headings in hierarchical order (H1, H2, H3...), with each level reflecting the section's depth in the page structure rather than its importance or visual size, and no skipped levels (e.g. H2 to H4)?
Do section headings succinctly describe the content that follows and make sense out of context (screen-reader users can pull up a list of headings), and are heading elements never empty?
How to check: Automated scan (empty headings) + content review + screen-reader headings list

Check: Are headings used consistently across pages (the same convention on every page of a type)?
Is all page content within an appropriate landmark element (header, nav, main, footer, search), with the page's unique content inside a main element?
Is each list of items, including navigation lists and menus, coded with HTML list elements (ul, ol, dl), with bullets styled in CSS rather than typed asterisks, dashes, numbers, or images?
How to check: Template review + content review (check that Markdown list markers actually render as ul/li)

Check: Are data tables marked up as tables, with row and/or column headers identified using th elements (not td cells made bold), and any caption inside a caption element?
Are tables used only for tabular data, never for layout?
Are complex tables (cells spanning rows or columns) and tables nested inside tables avoided?
Does the HTML pass a validation tool: elements tagged and nested properly, required attributes provided, id attributes unique?
How to check: Automated scan (Nu HTML Checker) of each template's output

Check: Does the page's content order make sense when read aloud by a screen reader (source/DOM order matches the visual order, including where CSS positions content, in multi-column layouts where each heading must be followed in the source by its own content, and where content is dynamically updated)?

Does each page have a unique, descriptive title that tells the user what the page is about and where they are in the site (e.g. Page Name | Section Name | Site Name), never empty and in plain text without HTML markup?
How to check: Template review + automated scan (duplicate or empty titles)

Check: Is link text clear and unique, describing where the link goes, and does it make sense out of context (screen-reader users may pull up a list of just the links)?
How to check: Content review + screen-reader or link-list tool

Check: Is generic link text like "read more" or "click here" avoided?
How to check: Automated scan + template review (news/event listing cards)

Check: Are links distinct from other text, using both color and underline (especially inline links)?
Is underlining reserved for links (non-link text is not underlined)?
Is the site navigation block (header, footer, menus) the same on every page where it appears: same place, same order and number of links, same appearance?
Are there multiple ways to locate pages (e.g. search, menu, breadcrumb, sitemap)?
Are menu items organized in a logical way with succinct labels?

Is the current page or section indicated in the navigation by more than color alone (e.g. an underline, which also survives High Contrast Mode and custom style sheets), and also to screen readers (e.g. visually hidden text "(the current page)")?
Is a "skip navigation" link available, and does it work (activate it, then Tab again)?
In long lists of links, are links the user has already followed (visited) shown, using the conventional link colors (Harvard advises against custom :visited colors)?
Do link phrases put key words at the beginning?
Is every page reachable through at least two methods (e.g. section menu and search), with no pages left outside the site's navigation structure?
If a site map is provided, is it kept up to date as the site changes?
How to check: Content review (or confirm it is generated automatically)

Check: Is the site navigation built on a nav element (or role="navigation") containing a list of links?
On pages with a lot of content, is there in-page navigation to sections (a nav region with a distinguishing aria-label such as "page sections", below the H1, linking to the section headings)?
Do areas outside the main content (navigation, sidebar) keep the same layout across all page types, and do similar pages use the same content layout?
How to check: Template review (compare every layout: news, events, people, programs)

Check: Do all links have the same appearance, without authors applying custom colors to individual links?
Can a visitor answer "Where am I and what can I do here?" on every page, with the most relevant resources obvious and easy to locate?
Is the contrast ratio between text and background at least 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text)?
How to check: Automated scan + contrast checker on every template's color pairs

Check: Where text is layered over a background with variation (photo or gradient), is it kept legible, e.g. with a solid-color layer between them?
Do icons, graphical objects, and user interface components (including button outlines) have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors?
Do highlighting effects such as link hover effects have sufficient contrast?
If a change in color alone identifies a selected or focused element, does that color change meet a 3:1 contrast ratio?
How to check: Template review (active filters, current menu item)

Check: Is color not the only way of conveying meaning, with an additional cue (icon or shape, pattern, border or outline, text, or dark/light value)?
How to check: Template + content review; view in grayscale / print in black and white

Check: Does the content avoid referring to items only by their visual appearance, size, position, or orientation?
Is very high contrast avoided (e.g. an off-white rather than white background)? (Harvard: "a good idea")
Can text be resized to 200% without loss of text or overlapping with other content?

At 200% zoom: is all content still present and in a sensible order, nothing overlapping or cut off, no horizontal scrolling, mobile-style menus navigable and closable, and links, buttons, forms and menus still working?
Does content reflow without loss of information or functionality and without scrolling in two dimensions (except content needing two-dimensional layout, such as maps, diagrams, video, data tables)?
Are relative units used for text size and container size (html font-size as a percentage, later sizes in em/rem, line-height relative or unitless) so browser text resizing works?
When spacing between letters, words, lines, or paragraphs is increased, does content stay readable, without overlapping or being hidden?
How to check: Manual test with a user style sheet / text-spacing bookmarklet

Check: Can the site's CSS be overridden by user style sheets that change headings, paragraph text, links and lists?
How to check: Manual test with a user style sheet

Check: Does content display and work in both portrait and landscape orientation (not locked to one unless essential)?
Does the layout adjust at large, medium and small viewport sizes without elements overlapping or crowding, and do fixed or sticky elements avoid obscuring content?
How to check: Manual test at several viewport widths

Check: Is body text left-aligned, with centered alignment only for headings and short strings, and justified alignment avoided?

Is body text limited to a comfortable width (around 60-100 characters per line), with a maximum paragraph width set so it doesn't grow too wide on wide screens, and are narrow columns of content avoided?
Is body text a comfortable size (18px is a good baseline) and is very small text (14px and under) avoided?
Is there plenty of line-height (1.3 to 1.5 for body text, depending on the font) and character spacing?
Are highly stylized fonts, italics, bold, and all caps used sparingly (all caps avoided)?
Does oversized text avoid truncating at small viewports or with user zoom settings?
How to check: Manual test at small viewport and zoom

Check: Is related content grouped, with headings, negative space between sections, and unnecessary clutter reduced?
Does the viewport meta tag allow pinch zoom on touch devices (no maximum-scale=1.0 or user-scalable=no)?
Is body text set in a clear, consistently formed and balanced sans-serif font? (Harvard: helps people with reading difficulties; not mandated)
Can all interactive elements be selected and activated using the keyboard?
How to check: Manual keyboard test of every template and widget

Check: Is nothing mouse-only (such as rollover menus); do toggles for hidden content work without hovering?
How to check: Manual keyboard test (header menus, share buttons, filters)

Check: Is the focus order logical, with source order matching the visual layout (e.g. a navigation bar shown at the top is also first in the source), without unexpected jumps to different parts of the page?
Is tabindex avoided on natively focusable elements, and never given a value greater than 0?

Is there a clear visible focus indicator on each link, button and custom control as it receives focus (the browser default not removed with outline:none unless replaced by a clear custom style, and without unexpected animated effects)?
How to check: Manual keyboard test + template review (search CSS for outline: none)

Check: Are inactive hidden controls (e.g. items in an unexpanded dropdown) removed from the focus order (hidden with display:none, not height:0/overflow:hidden), and do hidden-but-focusable controls (e.g. "skip to main content") become visible on focus?
Can each custom control receive focus (tabindex="0"), with currently inactive controls given tabindex="-1"?
When a custom control has focus, can it be activated with standard keys (button: Enter/Space, without Space scrolling the page; menu items: arrow keys; dialog dismissed with Escape)?
For dialogs that pop open: does focus move into the dialog and stay within it until it is dismissed, does Escape close it, and does focus return to the element that opened it?
If character-key shortcuts exist, can users turn them off or remap them, or are they active only when the component has focus?
Does every link have an href and no tabindex="-1" (unless it is deliberately disabled)?
How to check: Automated scan / template review (CSS a:not([href]) highlight)

Check: Does every form control have an accessible label, preferably visible text in an HTML label element associated with the control via for/id (or wrapping the control)?
How to check: Automated scan + template review (search box, listing filters)

Check: For a group of options (dropdown, radio buttons, checkboxes): is there a visible, meaningful label for the group and for each option (fieldset to group related questions)?

Does the label remain visible when the control has focus and while typing (placeholder text not used as the sole label: it isn't reliably read by screen readers, disappears on focus, and may have insufficient contrast)?

If a control has no visible text label (e.g. icon- or symbol-only buttons such as "×"): are there sufficient visual clues to its function, and a programmatic name (hidden label, aria-label, alt on an image inside the button, or title) that the screen reader reads?
How to check: Template review + screen-reader test (icon-only search button, close buttons)

Check: Where input has constraints or restricted formats, are they described in plain-language instructions?
Is the autocomplete attribute used on fields collecting common personal information (and turned off for sensitive information)?
How to check: Template review (if the site has any such form)

Check: Are required fields clearly indicated, visually without relying on color, and programmatically (e.g. aria-required, with any asterisk hidden from screen readers)?
When incorrect data is entered: is an error message displayed, on or near the field, that clearly explains the error and how to resolve it?
How to check: Manual test (if the site has any form with validation)

Check: Is each invalid input marked aria-invalid="true" and associated with its error message (aria-describedby), and are errors announced when the form is submitted (a live region saying the form has errors, or focus moved to the list of errors)?
Is semantic HTML used for controls (e.g. button for buttons)?
Are input fields clearly distinguishable from the surrounding area (border or contrasting background)?

Is the search placed above the main content (in or below the header and navigation), with the submit button right after the input and labeled with text (such as "search") rather than only a symbol or icon?
Are controls with potentially negative consequences (e.g. reset/clear) clearly differentiated and spaced apart from other controls?
Is each control big enough to operate (24x24px minimum, 44x44px recommended; at least 9.6mm across on a phone) and sufficiently spaced from neighboring controls?
How to check: Manual test on a smartphone + template review (footer links, share buttons, calendar days)

Check: Does the visible text label of each control match (or appear in the same word order in) its accessible name?
Does the text on each interactive element clearly describe the action or destination, with unambiguous icons?
Do buttons, form fields and other interactive components follow a consistent visual style that makes them recognizable and distinct from surrounding text?
Is there distinct visual variation between states: default, hover, focus, active/pressed, disabled?
Can each control be activated with a single pointer (no multipoint or path-based gesture required), and on the pointer or key up event?
Can functions triggered by moving the device also be operated by conventional controls?

For any embedded Qualtrics, Google or Microsoft form: accessible-contrast theme, form title set (shows in browser tab), no animated background or auto-playing music, and (Qualtrics) the Check Survey Accessibility tool run?

If search offers autocomplete suggestions: are the number of suggestions and how to choose them announced via a live region, can the options (listbox/option roles) be browsed with the up and down arrows, and does Enter select one and return focus to the input?

Is the search form inside a search landmark (a search element with role="search"), with a label on the input (visually hidden if needed) and any placeholder text in a darker gray than the browser default?
Does each control's visible hit area match its active area, so that everything that looks interactive is interactive (e.g. padding on the link itself, not its container)?
How to check: Template review + mouse/touch test (pagination, nav, cards)

Check: Is each custom widget (calendar, filters, menus, expandables) appropriate for its task, and does its behavior match a recognized accessible design pattern (WAI-ARIA, JS keyboard handling, CSS)?
How to check: Template review against the ARIA Authoring Practices patterns

Check: If a third-party UI library is used (e.g. for the calendar), has its documentation been checked for its out-of-the-box accessibility support and what must be added?
Does each custom control expose an accurate name, role, and current state or value, updated when you interact with it (e.g. a show/hide toggle or dropdown menu reflects whether its content is shown)?
Are toggles for hidden panels (dropdowns, drawers, modals, accordions, tabs) clearly labeled, keyboard accessible, not hover-dependent, and are sub-menus activated on click rather than hover?
How to check: Manual keyboard + mouse test (header menu, filter panels)

Check: Can content that appears on hover or focus (tooltips, sub-menus, popups) be dismissed without moving pointer or focus (e.g. Escape), stay visible while the pointer is over it, and remain until dismissed or no longer relevant?

Is dynamically updated content (e.g. "2 results returned" after filtering) identified in code as a live region or status message (role=status / aria-live) with a suitable priority (polite for feedback, so it doesn't override announcement of a focus change)?
How to check: Code inspection + screen-reader test (listing filters, calendar)

Check: Is focus moved only for alerts critical to the user's current activity, without otherwise forcing a focus change?
If a time limit is present: can users turn it off or change its length, and are they warned before it expires with an accessible prompt to extend it?
How to check: Template review (likely not applicable on a static site)

Check: Is each modal dialog marked up with role="dialog" and aria-labelledby/aria-describedby pointing to its title and description, with a close button whose accessible name is "close"?
How to check: Template review + screen-reader test (if the site has dialogs)

Check: Is each expandable section (accordion, collapsible filter panel) toggled by a real button (inside the heading, not the heading itself) that is in the focus order, works with Space and Enter, and exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls?
How to check: Template review + keyboard and screen-reader test

Check: Does every video posted on the site have synchronized, accurate closed captions, including proper punctuation, speaker identification, and meaningful sounds other than speech?
How to check: Content review by a person (every embedded video)

Check: Is caption accuracy at least that of a third-party captioning vendor such as 3Play Media (auto-generated captions, e.g. YouTube's, not relied on or published without substantial editing)?
Does every audio file or podcast have a full, accurate transcript, on the same page as the player or linked directly from the description text?

If a video includes visual-only information (on-screen text, graphics, actions not obvious from the audio), is it described in the script/audio or through audio description, or else is a transcript or text version of what happens in the video available on the same page?
How to check: Content review (close your eyes and listen)

Check: Is dense content shown in a video (data tables, visualizations, code, equations) also made available in accessible formats alongside it?
When video of a live event is later posted, are its captions corrected to post-production accuracy (punctuation, speaker names, non-speech sounds)?
Is any live stream embedded in a site page live-captioned by a professional captioner?
How to check: Content review (event pages with embedded streams)

Check: Do event listings include a statement that people can request accommodations (such as live captioning) in advance?
Does audio or video start playing only in response to a user action (no autoplay)?
Are all media player controls reachable and operable with the keyboard using standard keys, with a clear focus indicator?
How to check: Manual keyboard test, on more than one platform/device

Check: Does each player control have a descriptive name and a clear current state (e.g. Play/Pause conveys whether it is playing; the scrub control announces its time point)?
Can the player toggle the display of captions (with keyboard-accessible caption controls) and play audio descriptions?
For each video or animation, is there a way for users to pause or stop the moving content, and is moving or animated content used conservatively?
How to check: Manual test (animated hero images, carousels, embedded video)

Check: Is flashing or flickering content avoided, and if it is essential, is the flash rate outside the 2-55 Hz danger range, or is there a warning on links to the page?
Does all text in the visualization have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background?
Do adjacent data parts (bars, pie wedges) have 3:1 contrast against the background and each other, separated by a solid border color?
Is color not the only way meaning is conveyed (also a pattern, shape, or text label)?
Are the chart title, axes and other major elements labeled, with labels/legends (ideally direct labels) that clearly distinguish the data points?
Does the visualization have brief alt text or a longer description explaining the most important details (for complex graphs: categories, trends, maximum and minimum values)?
Is a supplemental format provided (data table or spreadsheet, or a longer description adjacent or in a collapsible section)?
Is the design familiar and simple, with animations avoided (or a way to turn movement off)?
For interactive visualizations: no interaction relies on hover, each data point is keyboard accessible, focus is visible, and zoom/font increase doesn't break the content?
Where text presents numbers or concepts that are hard to follow in prose (e.g. proportions), is a diagram or chart provided to illustrate them? (Harvard technique)
Is plain language used, avoiding jargon and figures of speech, fitted to the audience, with short words, sentences and paragraphs and redundant information removed?
Are acronyms spelled out on first use, and are definitions given for unusual words and abbreviations?
Is information in a logical order, with the important details first ("front-loaded")?
Is active voice used, with a clear actor?
Are changes of language marked in the page code so screen readers pronounce words correctly?
How to check: Content review + template review (lang attribute on passages)

Check: Is content broken into short paragraphs, lists and descriptive headings, avoiding extended blocks of unbroken text?
How to check: Content review; view with stylesheets off

Check: Scanning the page's overall "color": is it even, with only important elements (like headings) drawing attention?
Are terminology and design conventions used consistently across the site?
Does every page and element have a purpose that maps to the site's goals, with content unnecessary to the page's key purpose removed?
Does the text score around 60-70 on the Flesch Reading Ease scale (the target Harvard gives for an adult readership)?
How to check: Content review with a readability tool (Word readability statistics, TRAY for Chrome, Readability-Score.com, hemingwayapp.com)

Check: Do linked documents (Word, slides, PDF) meet accessibility guidelines, checked with built-in tools (Microsoft Accessibility Checker, Grackle, Adobe Accessibility Checker) or remediated by a vendor?
How to check: Content review of every linked document

Check: Where a PDF or other non-HTML format must be used, are all its available accessibility features provided?
Is any fillable PDF form replaced by an online form where possible (or made accessible)?
For each non-HTML document: are headings identified with a logical hierarchy, lists identified, and tabular data presented in tables?
How to check: Content review of every linked document

Check: Are PDFs generated from a source document (Word or ODF) that already has structure, rather than having structure added to the PDF afterwards?
Does each linked PDF have a Title set in its document properties?

Has the site been scanned with automated tools as a first step (Siteimprove, Harvard-licensed; or free tools: WAVE, Siteimprove Accessibility Checker extension, axe DevTools, Accessibility Insights for Web, ANDI)?
Have specific checks been run with HeadingsMap (heading outline) and the Nu HTML Checker (validation)?
Have color pairs been checked with a contrast tool (WebAIM Contrast Checker, Colour Contrast Analyser, Contrast Ratio; also Color Contrast Tool (APCA) and Contrast Grid for palettes)?
Have videos been checked for flickering and flashing content with the Photosensitive Epilepsy Analysis Tool (PEAT, Windows only)?
Has a manual content review been done (200% zoom, titles and headings, link text, plain language, images, color, forms, tables)?
Has keyboard-only testing been done (Tab, Shift+Tab, Space, Enter, arrow keys, Escape; in Safari enable "Press Tab to highlight each item")?
Has screen-reader testing been done (NVDA or JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on Mac), checking: is content skipped, is non-visible content read, are headings, links and buttons announced?
Have pages been viewed in grayscale (OS color filters) or printed in black and white to check nothing relies on color?
Have pages been viewed with stylesheets turned off (or listened to with a screen reader) to check headings, lists and content sequence?
Has content been usability-tested with people from the target audience to check it is meaningful and understandable?
Has an expert review by an experienced professional been considered (DAS can help identify reputable third-party providers)?
Has the page been read aloud to someone who isn't looking at the screen, to check that they get all the necessary information?
